title: Generative Forecasting from Coarse Observations: Does Cascading Help?
abstract: arXiv:2611.00686v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: We study probabilistic forecasting of dynamical systems such as fluids and waves from coarse observations. Since the unseen fine scales influence the dynamics, the same coarse initial state can evolve into a whole distribution of futures. Generative forecasters may produce visually plausible samples, but it is hard to tell whether they sample the right conditional distribution, since trajectory data contain a single future for each initial state. We address this problem by generating reference data in a hierarchical way: for each coarse initial state, we generate many different fine-scale components and numerically evolve the full states. translated_title: 从粗粒度观测进行生成式预测：级联有帮助吗？
translated_abstract: 我们研究从粗粒度观测中对流体和波等动力系统进行概率预测的问题。由于不可见的细尺度会影响动力学过程，同一个粗粒度初始状态可能演化出整个未来分布。生成式预测器可能产生视觉上合理的样本，但由于轨迹数据中每个初始状态仅包含单一未来，因此很难判断它们是否采样自正确的条件分布。我们通过分层方式生成参考数据来解决这一问题：对于每个粗粒度初始状态，我们生成许多不同的细尺度分量，并对完整状态进行数值演化。利用这些条件集合，我们表明标准的扩散模型和随机插值方法尽管在原理上是精确的，但在有限数据和模型容量下于整个预测时段上训练时，仍可能产生显著的分布误差。随后我们展示了级联较短的预测时段……
tldr: 该论文提出一种分层生成参考数据的方法来评估生成式预测器是否采样自正确的条件分布，发现标准扩散模型和随机插值在有限数据和模型容量下会产生显著的分布误差，并证明了采用级联较短预测时段的方式有助于缓解这一问题。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a hierarchical reference-data generation approach to evaluate whether generative forecasters sample the correct conditional distribution, reveals that standard diffusion models and stochastic interpolants incur substantial distributional errors under finite data and model capacity, and demonstrates that cascading shorter forecast horizons helps mitigate these errors.
